corrected_value.authors: Harrewijn, A., Abend, R., Naim, R., Haller, S. P., Stavish, C. M., Bajaj, M. A., et al.
corrected_value.title: Attention bias to negative versus non-negative faces is related to negative affectivity in a transdiagnostic youth sample.

decisions.quote: Second, to replicate and extend previous findings of Harrewijn et al. [15], we hypothesized that attention bias towards negative-valence face stimuli as measured with eye-tracking would be associated with facets of negative affectivity.
decisions.reason: The paper explicitly conducts two separate preregistered independent-sample replications: one re-testing Abend et al. (2020) [14] on anxiety-vs.-control group differences in eye-tracking dwell time (N = 105 independent sample, Table 2), and a second re-testing Harrewijn et al. (2021) [15] on the positive association between bifactor latent negative affectivity (NA) and trial-level dwell time on negative versus non-negative faces (N = 88 independent sample, Table 3, plus N = 185 combined sample, Table 4), concluding in the Discussion that neither study's hypotheses were replicated. Reference [15] in the source text verifies Harrewijn et al. (2021) in J Psychiatr Res 2021;138:514-8 (no DOI printed). The sole shipped row (input_row_index 1489) is Abend et al. (2020) (Res Child Adolesc Psychopathol 2020;49:227-40, DOI 10.1007/s10802-020-00712-w), which is a distinct original paper with a different sample (N = 53 vs. N = 97 transdiagnostic youth), analytic model, and empirical finding; report equivalence does not apply. No prior adjudication file existed for this work.
